key_insight: A Quantum Circuit Born Machine can generate useful synthetic tabular samples that improve minority-class learning in imbalanced datasets.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests quantum generative models may serve as a practical augmentation tool for structured data pipelines when classical oversampling is insufficient.
method: Normalize data and reduce dimensionality with PCA for basis encoding into a variational quantum circuit.
Train a QCBM by minimizing KL divergence with gradient-based parameter-shift optimization.
Generate synthetic minority samples and compare against SMOTE-family baselines on classification and distributional metrics.
evidence_signal: On Iris and Telco datasets, adding QCBM samples improved F1 by about 5–15% and minority recall by 10–25%, with only a 3–10% gap in cross-domain train/test evaluations and lower MMD on Telco than some classical methods.
watch_item: Results are strongest on low-dimensional tabular data, so scalability and encoding overhead may limit effectiveness on higher-dimensional or more complex datasets.
paper_title: Quantum-Enhanced Synthetic Data Generation Using Quantum Circuit Born Machines for Imbalanced Tabular Learning
